newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Athena says 96 profits up 93pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek Athena says 96 profits up 93pct.

text.p: Greek construction firm Athena's 96 pretax profit rose 93 percent to 500 million drachmas from 259 million in 1995, its financial manager told Reuters.
Turnover also more than doubled, reaching 6.0-6.5 billion drachmas from 3.0 billion in 1995, he said.

"Our company is currently involved in three large projects: the new Athens airport at Spata, the Rio-Antirio bridge and the port of Igoumenitsa in the western part of Greece," said financial manager Amvrosios Karatzas.
The company has signed two contracts for works on the Spata airport and expects to sign more, he said.
The Rio-Antirio bridge is a concession project. The French GTM-Doumez firm owns 55 percent and the remaining 45 percent is owned by six Greek construction companies.
The project is financed primarily by the European Investment Bank, which has expressed the view that in 30 years the bridge's cost will be totally recovered, Karatzas said.
The loan agreement will be signed by May 1 and construction, which will take between six to seven years, will begin immediately, he added.
The port of Igoumenitsa project has been budgeted at 15 billion drachmas and construction, which began in the summer of 1996, will end in 2001.
Athena has formed a joint venture with Spain's biggest construction company, FCC, for the completion of the project, Karatzas said.
Athena's orderbook of yet uncompleted projects stands at 40 billion drachmas he said.
